activities.title: Missing letters: bicycle
activities.content: You ride this two-wheeled vehicle to school: B_CYCLE.
activities.question: Type the missing complete word.
activities.explanation: Bicycle is spelled b-i-c-y-c-l-e.

activities.title: Compound noun: toothbrush
activities.content: Combine TOOTH and BRUSH to name an item used to clean teeth.
activities.question: Write the compound word.
activities.explanation: Toothbrush is a closed compound noun.

activities.title: Syllables: banana
activities.content: Arrange these syllables into a fruit: NA / BA / NA.
activities.question: Type the fruit.
activities.explanation: BA + NA + NA forms banana.

activities.title: Timekeeper
activities.content: I have two hands but cannot pick anything up. I have numbers on my face and hang on a wall.
activities.question: What am I?
activities.explanation: A wall clock has hands, a numbered face, and shows the time.

activities.title: Rainy day
activities.content: I stay folded on sunny days. In the rain, you hold me over your head.
activities.question: What am I?
activities.explanation: An umbrella opens to keep rain off a person.

activities.title: Reading helper
activities.content: I am small and thin. You put me between book pages so you can return to the right place.
activities.question: What am I?
activities.explanation: A bookmark keeps your place in a book.

activities.title: Meaning of thirsty
activities.content: After playing football, Maya drank two glasses of water.
activities.question: What does thirsty mean?
activities.explanation: Thirsty describes feeling a need to drink.

activities.title: Opposite of empty
activities.content: The glass has no water. It is empty.
activities.question: What is the opposite of empty?
activities.explanation: A full glass contains as much as it can hold.

activities.title: Choosing a verb
activities.content: Every morning, Sam ___ breakfast before school.
activities.question: Choose the correct verb.
activities.explanation: We say eat breakfast; with Sam (he), the present-simple form is eats.

activities.title: At the bakery
activities.content: You want two bread rolls. The baker asks, 'What would you like?'
activities.question: Choose the best reply.
activities.explanation: The reply names the item and uses please.

activities.title: Introducing yourself
activities.content: A new classmate says, 'Hello, I'm Tom. What's your name?'
activities.question: Choose an appropriate response.
accepted_answers_json: I'm Lina. Nice to meet you.
activities.explanation: A short introduction and friendly greeting answer the question.
activities.option_a: I'm Lina. Nice to meet you.

activities.title: Asking the time
activities.content: You have no watch and need to know the time. A teacher is nearby.
activities.question: What could you say?
accepted_answers_json: Excuse me, what time is it?
activities.explanation: Excuse me politely gets attention; the question asks for the time.
activities.option_a: Excuse me, what time is it?

activities.title: Train platform announcement
activities.learning_objective: Find a number in spoken information
activities.content: Listen to a short station announcement.
activities.question: Which platform is the train leaving from?
activities.explanation: The announcement explicitly says platform three.
activities.audio_transcript: Attention, passengers. The train to Green Park leaves from platform three at ten o'clock. Please stand behind the yellow line.

activities.title: A shopping request
activities.content: Listen to a short conversation about shopping.
activities.question: How many eggs does Noor need?
activities.explanation: Noor asks for six eggs.
activities.audio_transcript: Noor: Could you buy some eggs, please? Ali: Sure. How many do we need? Noor: Six eggs, please.

activities.title: Meeting at the library
activities.content: Listen to two friends planning to meet.
activities.question: What time will they meet?
activities.explanation: One friend suggests four o'clock and the other agrees.
activities.audio_transcript: Eva: Shall we meet at the library after school? Jay: Yes. Is four o'clock okay? Eva: Perfect. See you at four.

activities.title: The library notice
activities.content: Read this library notice.
activities.question: When does the library close?
activities.explanation: The notice states that the library closes at 5:00.
activities.reading_passage: City Library. Open Monday to Friday, 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Please return books at the front desk.

activities.title: A birthday message
activities.content: Read Mia's invitation.
activities.question: Which day is Mia's party?
activities.explanation: Mia says the party is on Saturday.
activities.reading_passage: Hi Ana! My birthday party is on Saturday at two o'clock. We will have cake and games in my garden. Please come! Love, Mia.

activities.title: A school reminder
activities.content: Read a reminder from the teacher.
activities.question: What should students bring?
activities.explanation: The reminder asks students to bring a notebook.
activities.reading_passage: Hello class. Tomorrow we will draw pictures of plants. Please bring a notebook and a pencil. I will bring the coloured pens. — Ms Reed

activities.title: Ordering water
activities.content: A customer is ordering at a café.
activities.question: Complete the customer's response.
activities.explanation: Yes, please accepts a polite offer.

activities.title: At the bus stop
activities.content: A passenger wants to check the bus route.
activities.question: Complete the passenger's question.
accepted_answers_json: Does this bus go to the museum?
activities.explanation: This is a clear yes/no question about the route.
activities.option_a: Does this bus go to the museum?

activities.title: After a greeting
activities.content: Two classmates greet each other.
activities.question: Choose the second student's reply.
activities.explanation: This is a natural response to 'How are you?'

dialogue_turns_json.speaker: Ava
dialogue_turns_json.text: Good morning, Liam. How are you?

activities.title: Ella's lost key
activities.content: Read a story about Ella finding her key.
activities.question: Where does Ella find her key?
activities.explanation: The story ends when Ella finds the key in her pocket.
activities.story_text: Ella comes home from school. She wants to open the door, but she cannot find her key. She looks in her bag and under her books. Then she checks her coat pocket. The key is there! Ella smiles and goes inside.

activities.title: The rainy picnic
activities.content: Read a story about a picnic.
activities.question: Where do the friends eat lunch?
activities.explanation: Rain makes the friends move their picnic inside the school.
activities.story_text: Ari, Jo, and Mei plan a picnic in the school garden. They make sandwiches and bring apples. At lunchtime, it starts to rain. The friends carry their food into the school. They sit near a window and enjoy their picnic together.

activities.title: The new puppy
activities.content: Read a story about a puppy named Max.
activities.question: What does Max carry to Ben?
activities.explanation: Max finds a red ball and takes it to Ben.
activities.story_text: Ben has a new puppy named Max. Max likes running in the garden. One morning, Ben throws a red ball. Max runs after it, picks it up, and brings it back to Ben. Ben smiles and gives Max a gentle pat.
